about:
Virginia Food Works operates a VDACS-inspected commercial kitchen at the Prince Edward County Cannery in Farmville, Virginia. The nonprofit organization was established to support Virginia farmers by providing a rental production facility for small-batch commercial retail co-packing during harvest season.

The facility offers appointment-based access to licensed equipment including kettles, mixers, fillers, and canners, with trained staff assisting clients through hot-fill, water-bath, and pressure canning processes. Production runs are scheduled Thursday through Saturday on a first-come, first-served basis, with peak demand from June through December. The kitchen specializes in acid and acidified foods—such as sauces, jams, relishes, and syrups—made from locally grown produce like tomatoes, berries, apples, peppers, and ginger root. Because of its regulatory scope, the facility cannot handle products containing meat, fish, or dairy.

Virginia Food Works serves both Virginia and out-of-state farmers looking to preserve seasonal harvests and reduce waste, as well as emerging small-business food entrepreneurs navigating commercial production for the first time. Clients range from growers creating value-added products for retail markets to startups needing guidance on recipe scaling, regulatory compliance, and process authority reviews. The organization also assists with VDACS registration and food safety training requirements.

The nonprofit's resource-first approach aims to strengthen Virginia's food system by helping producers transform perishable crops into shelf-stable goods that can be sold year-round, expanding market opportunities for local agriculture while keeping more food production within the state.
